title: 'Boogie Woogie Maxixe' and the Vic Ash session in London
summary: They settle the word as a Portuguese dance and correct the discography.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Okay. Finally, is the topic of discussion that came at the end of our first session which was when we talking about your recording session with Vic Ash in London in February of 1954.
You recorded the "Boogie Woogie Maxixe" or another possible pronunciation of that is Masheese, because I looked the word up, and it's, in fact, Portuguese.
Yeah. I thought it was French at the time.
It's a Portuguese dance. The lighter two-step. That's what my dictionary told me.
I think that's -- well it's got to be right.
We said that was an error
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

incidentally, in the discography. I supposed what we really mean is that the title of the tune ought to have been that. We don't know if that appeared on the record cover or whether it was actually Maxie.
So, somewhere along the line there was a mistake. Of course, now, it makes a lot more sense. 'Boogie Woogie Maxixe' doesn't signify anything too much.
